Figure 1 Comparison of MAS evolution paradigms. (Left) Search-based methods frame evolution as stochastic tree-branching (G0→Gi t) over full datasets, incurring low efficiency with insights isolated across branches. (Right) OptiMAS reformulates evolution as a data-driven continuous optimization over partitioned data (train/val/test), channeling action trajectories and accuracy as loss signals for OptiMAS to derive textual gradients and perform end-to-end MAS updates, yielding stable, sample-efficient, and overfit-resistant synthesis.

Figure 5 Architectural Topography of the Evolved Multi-Agent System (MAS) on SWE-Bench-Verified. This schematic contrasts the initial configuration E′ against the evolved architecture (E∗). Through our OptiMAS optimization, the system undergoes severe structural transformation: transitioning from a standard flat-worker scheme into a modular, hierarchical coalition composed of specialized agents (Worker, Reproducer, Refiner, and Verifier). Each sub-agent customized ReAct iteration budgets, and differentiated, priority-driven tool and skill allocations.
